sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 of the August 1890 Sanborn-Perris survey of Holly Beach City, the young resort on Five Mile Beach in Cape May County that is today the central part of Wildwood. Drawn at 60 feet to an inch, it covers the ocean side of the town between Pacific Avenue, which runs along the left edge of the sheet, and Ocean Avenue on the beach, and between Davis Avenue at the top and Hand Avenue at the foot. Atlantic Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, and the cross avenues Davis, Burke, Andrews, Taylor, Rio Grande and Hand divide it into two columns of numbered blocks with lots numbered from 101 to 244. Most lots are still vacant. The buildings are nearly all small frame dwellings and stores, with a Presbyterian church on Burke Avenue, the Philadelphia Hotel with a saloon, the Center House and a post office between Andrews and Taylor, a bakery, a pool room, a harness shop, a livery and carpenter's bench, the Cedars, Beach Villa and the Coleman House. On the beach front east of Atlantic Avenue are bath houses, the baths and pavilion of the S. S. & B. Improvement Companies at Taylor Avenue, and two buildings marked wrecked and damaged by waves, a record of storm damage at the ocean edge. The east side of Ocean Avenue is not drawn: the Atlantic Ocean is lettered there, together with the title cartouche giving a population of 1500 and no fire engines, the compass and the key. Blocks north of Davis Avenue and south of Hand Avenue are shown only in part; Pacific Avenue continues on sheet 23.
notes: Burke Avenue is today East Burk Avenue; the cross avenues east of New Jersey Avenue now carry the prefix East (East Davis, East Andrews, East Taylor, East Hand Avenue).
Two beach-front buildings between Taylor and Rio Grande Avenues are marked wrecked and damaged by waves.
Printed scale 60 ft to an inch; the fitted scale (6.62 px per ft) agrees with the scale bar.
Title cartouche: Sanborn-Perris Map Co., population 1500, no steam or hand engines, water facilities not good, prevailing winds S. and S.W.; New Jersey Coast Map Nos. 22 and 23.

Map, 60 ft to an inch. Pacific Av (left edge, cut near centre) to Atlantic and Ocean Avs (ocean side of Ocean Av not drawn); Davis Av to Hand Av (Davis, Burke, Andrews, Taylor, Rio Grande, Hand). Title cartouche, compass and key in the ocean area (masked). One part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 of the August 1890 Sanborn-Perris survey of Holly Beach City, today the central part of Wildwood, Cape May County. Drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the bay side is at the top, it covers the town west of Pacific Avenue: Arctic Avenue across the top, Holly Beach Avenue through the middle and Pacific Avenue along the foot, crossed by Hand, Rio Grande, Taylor, Andrews and Burke Avenues. Holly Beach Avenue carries the Pennsylvania Railroad line, drawn as a pair of tracks along its north side, and at its east end, beside a park east of Burke Avenue, stand the passenger depot and the freight depot. The blocks are cut into narrow numbered lots, most of them still vacant. Building is concentrated between Holly Beach and Pacific Avenues: scattered frame dwellings, a few stores and stables, the public school house on Andrews Avenue, the Barker Hotel and a cigar factory near Taylor and Andrews Avenues, and a dwelling with an observatory on Rio Grande Avenue. North of Holly Beach Avenue there are only a handful of dwellings. Narrow strips at the left and right edges show parts of the next blocks (31, 32 and 75), the top edge shows the first lots north of Arctic Avenue (blocks 166 to 170), and the foot repeats the edge of sheet 22, to which the ocean side of Pacific Avenue belongs. The street widths, 60 and 50 feet, are lettered in the streets.
notes: Holly Beach Avenue, with the railroad (lettered P. R. R.) in it, is today New Jersey Avenue; its junctions were hand-picked at the drawn street centre because the detector paired a rail with a street edge.
Burke Avenue is today West and East Burk Avenue; the other cross avenues carry West and East prefixes either side of New Jersey Avenue (Rio Grande Avenue excepted).
Passenger and freight depots stand in the park east of Burke Avenue.
Printed scale 60 ft to an inch; fitted 6.59 px per ft, consistent with sheet 22.

Map, 60 ft to an inch, turned (bay at top): Arctic Av to Pacific Av across Holly Beach Av (railroad in street; today New Jersey Av); Hand, Rio Grande, Taylor, Andrews, Burke Avs. Park with passenger and freight depots at right. One part.
